question: Why does a BlackICE 1937 save crash on load at hoi3_tfh.exe+0x4C42E1

addresses.name: CProvince_LoadKey_InfrastructureGate
addresses.comment:
`cmp dword ptr [ecx + 0x24], 0xC` where `ecx = building->effect (CBuilding +0xC)`, loaded one instruction earlier at 0x496125, inside CProvince::LoadKey's default (building-name) arm. **This is a MODIFIER id, not a building index.** The identical shape is already recorded in project.json at CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId (rva 0xB78AB), which reads `building->+0xC` and then compares `[eax+0x24]` against 0x2E, 0x2D, 0x4B, 0x0F and 0x66 - MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY, NAVAL_CAPACITY, LOCAL_AA, IC and LOCAL_UNDERGROUND - and the same comparison appears again in SetProvinceBuildingLevel at 0x4A3AED. Modifier 12 is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE (reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py), i.e. the building `infra`, so the write two instructions later makes `CMapProvince +0x5C` the province's infrastructure. This closes the blocker FINDINGS-power.md recorded as "which building type index 12 is was not established": `+0x24` was never a building index, so the mod's reordering of buildings.txt is irrelevant to it.

**Not only `infra` - corrected 2026-11-02.** The gate passes every building whose effect is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE, and the store at 0x496152 is a plain `mov [edi+0x5C]` with no comparison against what is there, so each such building in a province's block overwrites the last and **the last one wins**. With one such building in the base game the two readings could not be told apart. A save writes a province's buildings in `common/buildings.txt` order (14,189 of 14,189 blocks of a 1937 BlackICE save), so BlackICE's `extra_infra` (no. 60, `infrastructure = 0.05`) always follows `infra` (no. 21, 0.1) and a loaded province's figure is `extra_infra`'s level x 50. Read live in a full dump: Shanghai (5542, infra 8, extra_infra 1) 50, Leningrad (782, infra 9, extra_infra 2) 100, province 46 (infra 4, none) 400. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x496125-0x496152: cmp [ecx+0x24],0xC; jne; then level(+0x20) x [esi+8] / 1000 through the 64-bit helper and a plain mov [edi+0x5C],eax, no read of the old value. Live: full dump hoi3_tfh.exe.28460.dmp, CMapProvince +0x5C of 5542 = 50 and of 782 = 100 against the save's infra 8 and 9 and extra_infra 1 and 2. Would be wrong if a later pass rewrote +0x5C from infra before the dump; none of the five writers is a recompute from all buildings.
addresses.revises: 'i.e. the building infra' was an inference from the base game having one infrastructure building; any building with that effect writes it, last wins.

addresses.name: SetProvinceBuildingLevel
addresses.signature: void __fastcall SetProvinceBuildingLevel(CProvince* province@ESI, CBuilding* definition, int level, bool notify)
addresses.comment: 0x4A39B0-0x4A3B59, `ret 0xC`, receiver in **ESI**, three stack arguments. Trap 3: its first `ret 0xC` is at 0x4A3AD2 and the main path is the block after it, reached by the `jne 0x4A3AD5` at 0x4A39E1. It sets `province->buildings[definition->index]->level_max (+0x20)` and `level_current (+0x24)` to `level`, and then - **when the definition's modifier is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE, `definition->effect(+0xC)->id(+0x24) == 12`** - recomputes `province->+0x5C = level * definition->effect_size(+0x8) / 1000`. With `notify` set, when the old value was under g_FixedPoint0_200 and the new one over g_FixedPoint0_100, it calls **UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince (0x47F540)** with the province's own controller as both the old and the new one (0x4A3B22-0x4A3B33) - which joins a province in no area to its controller's and does nothing to one already in a real area, so **a fall in the figure never takes a province out of its area**; this was recorded as raising a message until 2026-11-02. The +0x5C store is plain, the last infrastructure building set winning (see CProvince_LoadKey_InfrastructureGate and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md), and finally rebuilds the province's modifiers through 0x49F3E0. Eight callers. **One of five writers of `CMapProvince +0x5C`**, which FINDINGS-power.md recorded as having exactly one - the others are CProvince::CProvince (0x494767, zero), the province building reset 0x496480 (0x496680, zero), CProvince::LoadKey (0x496152) and CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged (0x4B8024). Its opening also special-cases MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY (0x2D) on a province whose template +0xA4 is zero, reporting through 'province.cpp'. The name is from the body.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x4A3AED-0x4A3B41: the call target 0x47F540 is recorded as UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince; its arguments are esi and the pair (+0x334, +0x338) pushed twice. Would be wrong if 0x47F540's own record were wrong about doing nothing for equal ids in a real area.
addresses.revises: 0x47F540 is the area update, not a message; and the consequence for a falling figure.

addresses.name: RebuildOwnerAreas
addresses.comment: **Makes every area afresh.** ClearOwnerAreas, then for every country in the database's order and every province of its controlled list: where the province is simulated, in no area and has MaxInfrastructure above g_min_area_infrastructure, a new COwnerArea is made, flooded from it (COwnerArea::Flood) and appended to the country's list (+0xD30). When all are made, COwnerArea::BuildNeighbours on each. One caller, 0x648D48, inside CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler (0x6474A0): **areas are made afresh only when a game is entered, new or loaded**; in play only UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince moves a province. So a MaxInfrastructure overwritten in play (BlackICE's extra_infra) puts provinces in no area only at the next load - reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The caller address is already recorded; the containing function is the recorded CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler (0x2474A0-) by the record's own extents. Consistent with the full dump: 5542 in the null area at 50 although AI units held targets there from before the save.
addresses.revises: Names where the one caller is and what it implies.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_MayShipUnitToArea
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CAIUnit_MayShipUnitToArea(CAIUnit* agent, CUnit* unit, COwnerArea* area)
addresses.comment:
**Whether a unit may be given (or keep) a target in an area** - in effect, whether it has to cross water or hostile ground to get there. False when the area's region group (+0x6C, one side's land in one piece) is the group of the area of the unit's current province; when the area of its destination (or position) is real and landlocked (+0x68) or portless (+0x50 < 1) and CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(area's first province, unit, 1, 1) fails; when that destination is enemy-held, the unit CUnit::IsHoldingGround, retreats, or CAIUnit_UnitMayLeave(agent, unit, 0, 1, 1) refuses; when the area is enemy-held and army_role is 0 or 5; when it is not and army_role is 3 or 4 and (area +0x3C < 1 and it is not the acting capital's area, or the unit's own area COwnerArea_TouchesHostileArea). Otherwise AreaPair_SeaRouteOpen(own area, country, area). `ret 0xC`. Ghidra calls it CNullOwnerArea::CNullOwnerArea_3. Two callers in AssignAreaTargetsAndSealift (VA 0x8C584E keep-or-release, 0x8C5F98 candidates).

**It never tests the area's province count (+0x2C)**: it reads the head of `area`'s province list and dereferences it at 0x8C427B-0x8C4281 (for CanUnitReach, behind a slot-0 test of the destination's area, not this one) and at 0x8C42DB-0x8C42E1, unguarded. The keep-or-release caller (0x8C584E) passes the area of the unit's saved target with no test of its own, so a land unit bound for a province in no area - the CNullOwnerArea, empty - is a null read at rva 0x4C42E1. That is the load crash of 2026-11-02: two role-5 divisions, SOV's 27-y Ukrepl'onnyy Rayon bound for Leningrad (782) and CHI's Hubei Silingbu for Shanghai (5542), both put in no area by BlackICE's extra_infra. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md.
addresses.evidence: Two dumps of the crash: eip 0x8C42E1 (rebased), edx 0, ebx = g_null_owner_area read from the dump (VA 0x1A85574), return address 0x8C5853; the full dump names the units from [ebp-0x1C] and their targets from CArmy +0x2E8. Would be wrong if a caller tested slot 0 first; 0x8C5831-0x8C584E does not.
addresses.revises: Adds the missing count test and the crash it causes.

struct_fields.name: MaxInfrastructure
struct_fields.comment:
An int in thousandths that the unit AI uses as "is this province worth holding a front over". `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed` requires a neighbour's value to be at least 200 before the province counts as a front (0x4B8830), and gives the province itself the floor weight 500 instead of 1000 when its own value is at or below 300 (0x4B8BF4). Eight more readers across the unit AI and the map code. **Written in five places** (CProvince +0x5C lists them; this said one until 2026-11-02); the load's is `CProvince::LoadKey`'s default arm, which treats an unknown key as a building name and, when the loaded building's definition `+0x24` is 12, sets `province->+0x5C = building->level(+0x20) * definition->+0x8 / 1000` (0x96132-0x96152). Which building type index 12 is was **not** established - the mod reorders `common/buildings.txt`, so it is not safe to count. The cheapest live check is `dumpStruct.py` on a province and a comparison against the province panel.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02, and renamed from `ai_front_value`.** Read on every province with an `infra` key in `history/provinces/`, and compared: **10,642 of 10,642 agree** with `infra * 100`, where `infra` is the file's 0-10 value. (A first pass scored 98.43% against the *first* `infra` key in each file; all 167 misses were files that repeat the key, and the engine is **last-wins** - the residual was the test, not the field.) This does not contradict 'an int in thousandths': `infra * 100` and a fraction in thousandths are the same number, since the file's 0-10 is 0-100%. Paris (2613) reads 1000 = infra 10.0 = 100%.

**The old name named a use, not the field.** The unit AI reads infrastructure when deciding whether a province is worth holding a front over, which is why it looked like an AI value. The gain from the rename is that the thresholds become readable in the units a modder sees: the 200 at 0x4B8830 is **infrastructure 2.0** and the 300 at 0x4B8BF4 is **3.0**. A province under 2.0 does not count as a front; under 3.0 it gets the floor weight 500 instead of 1000.

`+0x24 == 12` is untouched by this and is still not a building index - `infra` is building no.21 in the mod's `common/buildings.txt`, so 12 is an id of something else, as the record already says.

**Renamed from `infrastructure` and retyped 2026-10-05, in step with CProvince +0x5C**, which is the same field: RTTI has CMapProvince deriving from CProvince at offset 0, and both structures carry it only because Ghidra has no inheritance. The game's own name is `MaxInfrastructure`, from `CProvince::GetMaxInfrastructure` (rva 0x6C360); the effective infrastructure is a different quantity computed by `CProvince::GetInfrastructure` (rva 0x94570) out of the modifier array at +0x114. The unit AI's use of this field - a neighbour needing at least 200 before a province counts as a front, the floor weight dropping to 500 at or below 300 - is unchanged by the rename and now reads as thresholds on 20% and 30% of full infrastructure, which is what the 1000 clamp in GetInfrastructure says the scale is.

**The value is the last infrastructure building's, not `infra`'s** (2026-11-02): LoadKey and SetProvinceBuildingLevel both store `level x figure / 1000` for whichever building with MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE they are handling, with no comparison, and a save writes buildings in `common/buildings.txt` order - so BlackICE's `extra_infra` (0.05 a level, after `infra`) leaves 1,603 of a 1937 save's 1,666 such provinces at 100 or under, which RebuildOwnerAreas then puts in no area. Live: Shanghai 50, Leningrad 100. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md.
struct_fields.evidence: As for CProvince_LoadKey_InfrastructureGate; the five writers are those CProvince +0x5C's record already names.
struct_fields.revises: 'Written in exactly one place' contradicted CProvince +0x5C's own record; adds that the last infrastructure building wins.

struct_fields.name: MaxInfrastructure
struct_fields.comment:
The same field project.json records on CMapProvince; both structures carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two. It is written by CProvince's own code - zeroed in CProvince::CProvince at 0x494767 and in the province building reset at 0x496680, computed in CProvince::LoadKey at 0x496152, in SetProvinceBuildingLevel at 0x4A3B0A and in CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged at 0x4B8024 - and the full account is on the CMapProvince entry.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02** against 10,642 provinces' `infra` keys in `history/provinces/` - 100.00% agree with `infra * 100`. `CMapProvince +0x5C`'s entry, which used to carry the name `ai_front_value`, is now named `infrastructure` to match this one.

*This used to point at a `FINDINGS-infrastructure.md`, which has never existed - not in the tree and not anywhere in git history. The evidence for the name is the sentence above, not a document. Found 2026-10-05, when checkrefs.py learned to read this file; the dead pointer is removed rather than repaired because there is nothing to repair it to.*

**Renamed from `infrastructure` and retyped 2026-10-05: it is the maximum, and the game has a separate accessor for the effective figure.** `CProvince::GetMaxInfrastructure` (rva 0x6C360) copies +0x5C out as a `CFixedPoint`, while `CProvince::GetInfrastructure` (rva 0x94570) is a different and much longer function that does not read +0x5C at all: it takes the province's modifier array at +0x114 and computes `values[MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE] * (1000 + values[LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE] + values[GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE]) / 1000`, floors it at a cached constant and clamps it at 1000. Two accessors, two quantities, and only one of them is this field. The clamp at 1000 also fixes the scale: with the recorded live check - 100.00% of 10,642 provinces' `infra` keys agreeing with `infra * 100` - the field is thousandths of full infrastructure, 1000 being 100%, and `infra = 10` in history is the maximum.

**The value is the last infrastructure building's, not `infra`'s** (2026-11-02): LoadKey and SetProvinceBuildingLevel both store `level x figure / 1000` for whichever building with MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE they are handling, with no comparison, and a save writes buildings in `common/buildings.txt` order - so BlackICE's `extra_infra` (0.05 a level, after `infra`) leaves 1,603 of a 1937 save's 1,666 such provinces at 100 or under, which RebuildOwnerAreas then puts in no area. Live: Shanghai 50, Leningrad 100. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-extrainfra.md.
struct_fields.revises: Adds that the last infrastructure building wins, and what that does to areas.
